free_tier.stated: The free SteadIP tier is HTTP and HTTPS only, so it does not answer test: "Free users get a random subdomain" and "SteadIP focuses on HTTP and HTTPS first". The IPv4 product is paid: "$29.99 USD per dedicated IPv4 address, billed annually."

egress.terms: No transfer allowance and no fair-use figure are published in the announcement, the product explainer or the homepage. The plan is priced per address per year only.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: Config file plus a customer panel for ports and an optional hostname.
tooling: wg-quick; an optional hostname under steadip.com
chaining: Pairs with the vendor's own free HTTP tunnel: one address for raw TCP and UDP, one hostname for the website.
binding_note: Nothing published fails at 1 TiB/month except an unknown volume policy, so the honest answer is that the wall is undocumented. At USD 29.99 per year for a whole IPv4 the price is not the wall.

identity_cost.detail: A SteadIP account plus a paid annual add-on; the site sells a separate "Verified" tier at USD 19.99 per year, which suggests verification is a paid product rather than an identity check. The signup form was not read.

reliability_note: Nothing published on throttling, bans or drop behaviour; the free HTTP tier and the paid Anchor product share a vendor whose main product is an frp-based tunnel.
confidence_note: Price, the config file and both inbound modes are first-party. Two gaps: which mode the Anchor add-on includes, and any volume figure. A support question would close both.

evidence.proved: USD 29.99 per year per dedicated IPv4, about USD 2.50 per month; the address is assigned to the account rather than shared
WireGuard config supplied by the vendor; Starter forwards selected ports, Pro and Business offer 1:1 NAT for all ports
the free tier is HTTP and HTTPS with a random subdomain; the paid tunnel tier is USD 19.99 per year

price_per_tb_month: USD 29.99 per year per dedicated IPv4 (about USD 2.50 per month)
notes: Cheapest whole IPv4 found at USD 29.99 per year, and the only one whose free tier is honestly HTTP-only rather than an IPv6 substitute. Which inbound mode the Anchor add-on gets is not stated, and that decides whether every port is open or a few are forwarded. The steadip.com/anchor page returned a broker refusal on two attempts, so the blog announcement is the source.

extras.wg_detail: "We provide a WireGuard config. You import it on a router, server, VM, or even a desktop." Inbound is either selected ports or all of them: "Port forwarding: forward only the ports you want" or "Forward all ports (1:1 NAT): true full inbound reachability (all ports)".
extras.volume_stated: No transfer allowance and no fair-use figure are published in the announcement, the product explainer or the homepage. The plan is priced per address per year only.
extras.transit_note: The vendor's gateway carries the address and terminates the tunnel; the client's ISP only sees outbound.
